picks.editorial_note: AI system designed by Mario Krenn's team proposes novel physics experiments that outperform human-designed setups, published in Nature — a striking demonstration of AI accelerating fundamental scientific discovery itself.
picks.title: Artificial Intelligence Suggests New Physics Experiments

picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen's international team published 'HydroGym' in Nature, an RL platform that trains AI agents to control fluid dynamics across energy, transportation, and defense applications — a physics-informed breakthrough with broad engineering reach.
picks.title: Training AI Agents that Can Actively Control Fluid Dynamics in Energy, Transportation, and Defense | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: HKUST's GSCo framework pairs a generalist medical AI with lightweight specialist models to improve precision healthcare diagnostics, a meaningful architectural advance for deploying AI safely in clinical settings.
picks.title: Novel AI Framework Unites Generalist and Specialist Models for Precision Healthcare
picks.university: Hong Kong Univ. of Science and Technology

picks.editorial_note: EPFL researchers trained LLMs to express calibrated uncertainty when proposing experiments, improving automated scientific discovery pipelines — a step toward AI systems that know what they don't know.
picks.title: An AI capable of doubt can optimize scientific discovery

picks.editorial_note: NSF is funding a new $30 million Science and Technology Center, led by Michigan State with Georgia Tech among eight partners, to advance predictive modeling of turbulence — a major multi-institution investment in foundational science.
picks.title: New Center Seeks to Unlock the Science of Turbulence for Energy, Flight, and Discovery

picks.editorial_note: The Department of Energy awarded a University of Houston-led coalition $2.88M to use AI for discovering next-generation permanent magnets, directly targeting America's critical mineral supply chain vulnerabilities.
picks.title: Department of Energy Awards UH-led Team $2.88M to Use AI to Strengthen America’s Critical Mineral Supply Chain | University of Houston

picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen spin-off Black Semiconductor won a major engineering award for graphene-based chips that transmit data optically instead of electrically, a technology transfer success with real commercialization momentum.
picks.title: Light Instead of Electricity: Aachen Engineering Award for a Technological Breakthrough | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: Helmholtz researchers argue Germany and Europe must build sovereign open frontier AI models rather than depend on US and Chinese systems — a policy stance with direct implications for European AI research strategy.
picks.title: Why we in Germany and Europe need to build our own open frontier models

picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen's autonomous research vehicle 'karl.' received a nationwide German testing permit, a regulatory milestone that opens the door to broader public-road autonomous vehicle research in Europe.
picks.title: RWTH Receives Nationwide Testing Permit for Autonomous Research Vehicle “karl.” | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: Federal agency AHRQ cancelled a Johns Hopkins AI-driven healthcare research grant amid broader funding cuts, illustrating how shifting federal policy is directly disrupting AI research aimed at improving diagnosis timelines.
picks.title: Funding cuts hit research focused on making American healthcare safer, more efficient
